title: Pterostilbene targets microglia-mediated neuroinflammation for Alzheimer's therapy.
authors: Chen, Feichi; Lv, Xinhuang; Xiang, Kun; Lin, Xiaoou; Dai, Conghui; Wei, Chuhua; Zhang, Yang; Liu, Jiaming; Li, Jing
one_liner_zh: 该文研究紫檀芪通过JAK2-STAT3通路抑制小胶质细胞介导的神经炎症治疗阿尔茨海默病，虽含分子对接与MD模拟，但对象为药物-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Microglia-mediated neuroinflammation is a key driver of Alzheimer's disease (AD) progression, exacerbating neuronal damage and pathological changes. Pterostilbene (PTE), a natural anti-inflammatory stilbenoid, shows neuroprotective potential in AD, but its specific mechanism in regulating AD-related neuroinflammation remains unclear. Here, we explored the anti-neuroinflammatory effect and mechanisms of PTE against AD. APPswe/PS1dE9 (APP/PS1) transgenic mice were treated intragastrically with PTE for 4 weeks, followed by evaluation of cognitive function and pathological changes. Amyloid-beta burden, Tau protein phosphorylation, microglial activation, and proinflammatory cytokines production were analyzed. To further investigate the potential mechanism of PTE, an integrated approach combining network pharmacology, RNA sequencing, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and cell transfection techniques were conducted. Our results showed that PTE treatment improved cognitive impairment, amyloid-beta deposits, Tau protein phosphorylation, microglia activation, and production of tumor necrosis factor-alpha, interleukin-1beta, and interleukin-6 in vivo and in vitro. Notably, molecular docking predicted that PTE has binding affinity for Janus kinase 2 (JAK2) at LYS-857, LYS-882, and LEU-932. Consistently, site-directed mutagenesis reduced the inhibitory effect of PTE on JAK2/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) phosphorylation, supporting JAK2 as a functional target. Meanwhile, we revealed that PTE effectively inhibited activation of microglia in the APP/PS1 mice by regulating JAK2-STAT3 pathway. These findings indicate that PTE treatment could attenuate microglia-mediated neuroinflammation via regulating JAK2-STAT3 signaling pathway, which might provide a novel option to elucidate the effects of PTE on AD.
abstract_zh: 小胶质细胞介导的神经炎症是阿尔茨海默病（Alzheimer's disease, AD）进展的关键驱动因素，加剧神经元损伤和病理变化。紫檀芪（Pterostilbene, PTE），一种天然抗炎性二苯乙烯类化合物，在AD中显示出神经保护潜力，但其在调节AD相关神经炎症中的具体机制仍不清楚。在此，我们探讨了PTE对抗AD的抗神经炎症效应及其机制。APPswe/PS1dE9（APP/PS1）转基因小鼠经灌胃给予PTE治疗4周，随后评估认知功能和病理变化。分析了淀粉样蛋白-β负荷、Tau蛋白磷酸化、小胶质细胞激活及促炎细胞因子产生。为进一步研究PTE的潜在机制，采用了结合网络药理学、RNA测序、分子对接、分子动力学模拟和细胞转染技术的综合方法。我们的结果表明，PTE治疗在体内和体外均改善了认知障碍、淀粉样蛋白-β沉积、Tau蛋白磷酸化、小胶质细胞激活以及肿瘤坏死因子-α、白细胞介素-1β和白细胞介素-6的产生。值得注意的是，分子对接预测PTE对Janus激酶2（Janus kinase 2, JAK2）在LYS-857、LYS-882和LEU-932位点具有结合亲和力。一致地，定点突变降低了PTE对JAK2/信号转导与转录激活因子3（signal transducer and activator of transcription 3, STAT3）磷酸化的抑制作用，支持JAK2作为功能性靶点。同时，我们揭示PTE通过调节JAK2-STAT3通路有效抑制了APP/PS1小鼠中小胶质细胞的激活。这些发现表明，PTE治疗可通过调节JAK2-STAT3信号通路减轻小胶质细胞介导的神经炎症，这可能为阐明PTE对AD的作用提供一种新选择。
